messages:
elaine: quick q re: prefetch window granularity — are we comfortable with 50ms buckets? i'm seeing eviction churn spike on heavy multi-tenant runs and it looks correlated with p95 request latency.
chris: 50ms is a decent middle ground. smaller windows (20ms) reduce wasted prefetch but increase churn and CPU overhead. bigger windows (100-200ms) cut churn but hurt p95 for interactive flows.
vinh: we could make it adaptive: start narrow for hot prefixes, widen for cold. but that adds complexity to the controller + telemetry surface.
sam: do we have the exact metrics to tie eviction churn -> tail latency? i can run an experiment but need the metric names and a test harness.
chris: metrics to look at: kv.prefetch.eviction_rate, kv.prefetch.prefetch_count, kv.latency.p50/p95/p99 per-tenant. also trace heatmaps for prefix hotness.
maria: proposal: per-tenant prefetch_window_ms + a global grace policy. e.g.
```
prefetch:
  default_window_ms: 50
  per_tenant_override:
    hot: 20
    bulk: 200
  grace_eviction_ms: 500
```
vinh: i worry per-tenant overrides encourage manual tuning. prefer an admission/credit system: give hot tenants prefetch credits and drain on eviction pressure.
chris: admission + adaptive windows sound good together. also watch batching_window interaction — if batching_window_ms is large, a small prefetch_window is wasted because requests are coalesced later. e.g., batching_window_ms=10 can pair well with prefetch_window_ms=30.
elaine: good call. can we scope an experiment: compare (20ms,50ms,150ms) across 3 tenant classes (hot, normal, bulk) for 24h on canary? @sam can you run it and collect the metrics you mentioned?
ops-bot: deploy: prefetch-proto v3 -> canary-2 @ 7401234585 :rocket:
sam: yep i'll kick off the run today. i'll also capture kv.cache.hit_ratio and tenant-fairness score (we talked about that last week).
maria: one more correctness note: prefetch mustn't violate read-after-write ordering for recent writes. ensure prefetch respects prefix pin tokens or uses a short validation read before serving.
vinh: agreed — prefetch should be conservative on prefixes with recent mutations. a small TTL since last-write could gate prefetch eligibility.
elaine: ok action items:
- sam: run the (20/50/150) experiment + telemetry by EOD tomorrow
- chris + vinh: sketch adaptive-window + admission design doc (small RFC)
- maria: add read-after-write validation bullet to prefetch checklist
thanks, everyone :thumbsup:
